The three public-user defects (SKIP != FAIL, env-overridable corpora, stop-pair topic seeds) ship in sweep-v3.44. STANDING RULES carried from phase 3 (S25), still enforced every run: the flow is EVIDENCE → SYNTHESIS → CONTRARIAN → ADJUDICATION → VERDICT → VERIFICATION; every synthesis claim resolves SUPPORTED / PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED / UNSUPPORTED / CONTRADICTED / UNDECIDABLE against a frozen evidence snapshot; declared role identity never proves underlying model weights — that limitation stays UNKNOWN and is recorded, never claimed away.
hard_rules: The SYNTHESIZER may never adjudicate its own conclusion.
No confidence score may substitute for evidence — the field is refused outright.
A claim with no evidence-node provenance MUST be rejected.
A contradiction between evidence and claim MUST automatically block promotion until resolved.
The ADJUDICATOR must be independently versioned from the SYNTHESIZER: model identity, model version, prompt/config hash, timestamp, evidence snapshot hash.
Role separation must be enforced through machine-readable artefacts and promotion rules — never a written rule as the primary defence.

Two different prompts do NOT constitute independence, and two API calls never prove different underlying model weights: the independence ladder is DECLARED_IDENTITY → OBSERVED_EXECUTION → VERIFIED_CONFIGURATION → UNKNOWN_UNDERLYING_WEIGHTS, and a record claiming more than it can prove is refused as an overclaim.

known_blockers_found_by_inspection.finding: The declared pipeline ORDER was COMPARISON → CONTRARIAN → SYNTHESIS, so the synthesizer received the contrarian's objections BEFORE producing its conclusion. Attack A51 was the default.
known_blockers_found_by_inspection.resolution: RESOLVED — ORDER is now …COMPARISON → SYNTHESIS → CONTRARIAN → ADJUDICATION → VERDICT → VERIFICATION; SYNTHESIS's contract forbids contrarian.jsonl as an input; adjud.synthesis_blind proves absence from the synthesis snapshot's files_present.
known_blockers_found_by_inspection.consequence: RESOLVED — do not reintroduce COMPARISON → CONTRARIAN → SYNTHESIS ordering; adjud.synthesis_blind will refuse it (A51).

known_blockers_found_by_inspection.finding: In the synthetic control case the CLAIM node was created INSIDE the CONTRARIAN stage — the stage meant to attack the claim was the stage that materialised it. No record existed of who authored what.
known_blockers_found_by_inspection.resolution: RESOLVED — every CLAIM is authored by the SYNTHESIZER and every COUNTERCLAIM by the CONTRARIAN, recorded in the node's author field and enforced by adjud.node_authorship.
known_blockers_found_by_inspection.consequence: RESOLVED — do not let CONTRARIAN materialise a CLAIM node, or SYNTHESIZER a COUNTERCLAIM; adjud.node_authorship will refuse it.

known_blockers_found_by_inspection.finding: Model identity was unrepresentable — no model name, version, prompt hash or config hash anywhere in the system.
known_blockers_found_by_inspection.resolution: RESOLVED — declareRole() records {role, model, model_version, prompt_sha256, config_sha256} as a chained ROLE_DECLARED event (inside the run seal via events_head) and in the manifest; the two must agree (adjud.roles_declared).
known_blockers_found_by_inspection.consequence: RESOLVED — do not add a role or stage without declareRole(); adjud.roles_declared will refuse an undeclared or mismatched identity.

known_blockers_found_by_inspection.finding: Claims had no per-claim status — verdict.json carried truth at the VERDICT level only.
known_blockers_found_by_inspection.resolution: RESOLVED — synthesis.json declares claims[] with ids and cites; adjudication.json resolves each id with one of the five values plus supporting/contradicting node references (adjud.claims_resolved, adjud.record_valid).
known_blockers_found_by_inspection.consequence: RESOLVED — do not let a verdict ship without adjudicating every synthesis claim; adjud.claims_resolved will refuse it.

known_blockers_found_by_inspection.finding: A43 (synthesizer and adjudicator secretly the same model) cannot be fully closed from inside this repo: distinct declared identity and distinct execution records are enforceable; proving two API calls reached different weights is not.
known_blockers_found_by_inspection.resolution: BOUNDED, permanently — the independence ladder ends at UNKNOWN_UNDERLYING_WEIGHTS, the adjudication record must say so, and a record claiming weight independence is refused as an overclaim (validated in sonar-adjudicate.js --selftest).
known_blockers_found_by_inspection.consequence: BOUNDED, not solvable — never write a record claiming proven weight-independence; validateAdjudication() refuses the overclaim by design.
